hero.title: Welcome to Your UI Plugin
hero.subtitle: Your plugin renders as a native micro-frontend inside Identity Security Cloud; it rides the tenant's session and security model, so there is no separate login and nothing extra to host. Explore the examples, then make it your own.

overview.heading: Build native experiences inside Identity Security Cloud
overview.intro: Your plugin renders as a micro-frontend right inside Identity Security Cloud. It rides the tenant's session and security model, so there is no separate login, no external hosting, and nothing extra to secure.
overview.whatItem1: Dashboards that bring together data from any Identity Security Cloud API
overview.whatItem2: One-click workflow launchers that kick off your business processes
overview.whatItem3: Admin tools tuned to your organization's governance needs
overview.patterns: The pages in this template show the patterns you will use every day: reading plugin context, calling Identity Security Cloud APIs with typed SDK services, and launching workflows through the Launchers API.
overview.gettingStartedBody: This template is yours to reshape. The SDK wiring in core/ handles the App Shell handshake, so components simply read signals and call services. Open the Workflows tab to see how to list and start launchers, and the API Examples tab for the Observable and Promise patterns when calling Identity Security Cloud APIs.

workflows.heading: Workflow Launchers
workflows.intro: UI plugins can start SailPoint Workflows through the Launchers API. This page lists launchers assigned to you (via Launchpad) and lets you start one. The workflow runs server-side; the plugin receives an Interactive Process ID that links to the Launchpad for any interactive steps.
workflows.emptyState: No launchers found. Launchers are assigned to users through the Launchpad configuration in Identity Security Cloud. If you expect to see launchers here, verify your Launchpad assignments.

apiExamples.heading: API Examples
apiExamples.intro: The SailPoint Angular SDK provides typed services for calling ISC APIs. This page demonstrates two patterns: Observable (for reactive pipelines and template binding) and Promise (for event handlers and sequential chains).
apiExamples.observableBody: IdentitiesService.listIdentitiesV1() returns an Observable. Use it with AsyncPipe for automatic subscription management. A gate signal controls when the Observable is subscribed.
apiExamples.observableHint: Prefer Observables when: binding results directly to templates, chaining multiple async operations reactively, or when you need cancellation on component destroy.
apiExamples.promiseBody: TenantService.getTenantV1() wrapped with firstValueFrom() converts the Observable to a Promise. Useful for event handlers and async/await chains.
apiExamples.promiseHint: Prefer Promises when: responding to user actions in event handlers, writing sequential async logic, or integrating with Promise-based libraries.
